knowledge_delta.summary: The Transformer source opens a new neural sequence-architecture branch. All five scaffold-retrieved project concepts are rejected as cross-domain noise rather than forcing later learning/agent/governance ideas into the 2017 paper.

items.label: Transformer sequence-transduction architecture
items.source_basis: The paper proposes an encoder-decoder architecture based solely on attention mechanisms, dispensing with recurrence and convolution for sequence transduction.
items.prior_basis: The graph had agent/runtime, learning and data-system concepts but no neural sequence-transduction architecture.
items.interpretation: The original Transformer is modeled as its 2017 encoder-decoder architecture rather than being retroactively collapsed into the broader modern LLM category.

items.label: Self-attention
items.source_basis: Encoder self-attention lets each encoder position attend to all positions in the previous layer; decoder self-attention does the same under a future-position mask.
items.prior_basis: No prior project concept represents neural attention among sequence positions.
items.interpretation: Self-attention becomes a neural sequence mechanism, separate from ReAct observation feedback or human attention/retrieval concepts.

items.label: Sequence-computation parallelism
items.source_basis: Table 1 compares full self-attention at O(1) sequential operations per layer with recurrent layers at O(n), one of the paper's main motivations for attention-only sequence layers.
items.prior_basis: No prior concept models neural sequence parallelism created by removing recurrent layer dependencies.
items.interpretation: Parallelism is retained as a specific computational-graph advantage, not as a claim that autoregressive output generation becomes fully parallel.

items.label: Attention dependency path
items.source_basis: Table 1 gives full self-attention O(1) maximum path length between positions versus O(n) for recurrent layers.
items.prior_basis: The graph has causal/process relations but no neural-network path-length model for sequence dependencies.
items.interpretation: Short dependency paths are kept as a separate reason self-attention can help long-range dependency learning rather than merged with generic performance claims.

items.label: Positional encoding
items.source_basis: Because the model contains no recurrence and no convolution, the paper adds positional encodings to input embeddings so sequence order is represented.
items.prior_basis: No prior project concept describes explicit positional information in an attention-only neural sequence model.
items.interpretation: Removing recurrence creates a new responsibility: order is no longer supplied by the recurrence structure and must be injected explicitly.

claims.text: The 2017 paper proposes the Transformer as an encoder-decoder sequence-transduction architecture based on attention mechanisms rather than recurrent or convolutional sequence layers.
The original Transformer uses encoder self-attention, masked decoder self-attention and encoder-decoder attention as distinct attention roles inside an encoder-decoder model.

In Table 1, full self-attention has O(1) sequential operations and O(1) maximum path length versus O(n) and O(n) for recurrence, while self-attention's per-layer sequence cost is O(n²·d) rather than recurrent O(n·d²).

evidence.locator: PDF Table 1 and §4 Why Self-Attention p.6

claims.text: Because the Transformer contains neither recurrence nor convolution, the paper adds positional encodings to token embeddings so the model can use sequence order.
Decoder self-attention is masked to prevent positions from attending to future output positions, preserving the autoregressive property despite removal of recurrent layers.

The paper's primary empirical evidence is WMT 2014 English-to-German and English-to-French machine translation, with additional constituency-parsing experiments rather than modern decoder-only LLM benchmarks.

The original paper should not be treated as direct evidence for every later decoder-only LLM architecture or current performance claim; those are later developments beyond the encoder-decoder translation architecture and 2017 experiments reported here.
claims.note: This is the project's scope boundary: it compares what the 2017 source actually specifies and evaluates with later terminology, without attributing later LLM developments to the paper.

prerequisite_map.summary: The model is reconstructable once the reader understands the original Transformer architecture, self-attention, the parallelism/path-length argument and why removing recurrence makes position an explicit input.

items.label: Transformer sequence-transduction architecture
items.reason: Without the original encoder-decoder scope, later decoder-only LLM architecture is easily projected backward into claims the paper did not make.

items.label: Self-attention
items.reason: This is the central sequence mechanism that replaces recurrent state propagation inside the Transformer encoder and masked decoder layers.

items.label: Sequence-computation parallelism
items.reason: The paper's architectural leverage depends on understanding which recurrent sequential dependencies disappear from layer computation.

items.label: Attention dependency path
items.reason: Short paths between distant positions are a separate motivation from parallelism and explain why attention changes long-range dependency modeling.

items.label: Positional encoding
items.reason: Once recurrence and convolution disappear, order no longer comes from the sequence-processing structure and must be represented explicitly.

learning_prompt.retention_prompt: Without looking back, reconstruct the original Transformer argument: what recurrent sequence dependency it removes, how self-attention changes layer parallelism and maximum dependency path, what quadratic sequence-length cost remains, why positional encoding is required, and which parts of the model/evidence belong specifically to the 2017 encoder-decoder translation context.

transfer_prompt.prompt: A colleague says 'Transformers are faster because attention is O(1) and all generation is parallel.' Use the 2017 paper's own comparison to correct the statement: which sequential dependency is O(1), what O(n²) cost remains, and why the masked decoder is still autoregressive?

source_decision.rationale: The explainer preserves the original attention-only mental model and its 2017 scope, but the paper is still worth skimming at the architecture, Table 1/Why Self-Attention and machine-translation-result sections because these are exactly where modern summaries often flatten the encoder-decoder design, the quadratic cost trade-off and the historical evidence boundary.

novelty.reason: The paper opens a new neural sequence-architecture branch; all scaffold-retrieved concepts were false cross-domain matches rather than prior knowledge to refine.

source_quality.reason: This is the original primary research paper and arXiv record for the Transformer architecture and reported experiments.

relevance.reason: The architecture is foundational for understanding modern language models, provided the original encoder-decoder and task scope remains explicit.

practical_leverage.reason: The parallelism/path/cost decomposition is reusable for evaluating sequence architectures and avoiding simplistic Transformer explanations.

compression_loss.reason: The core model compresses well, but exact attention roles, Table 1 trade-offs and the original experiment scope are worth verifying in the paper because they are frequently distorted by later terminology.
